title: About House of Guidance
text: House of Guidance is a community dedicated to Qur'an, Arabic, and Islamic education — teaching with structure, patience, and sincerity. Vision: A community where every Muslim has the means to read, understand, and live by the Qur'an. Mission: To provide accessible, structured Islamic education — from first letters of Arabic to Tajweed and memorization — rooted in sound teaching and good character. Objectives: Teach the Qur'an with correct Tajweed, from beginner to advanced levels; Build a supportive learning community for Arabic and Islamic studies; Support Hifzh students with structured, sustainable memorization; Share authentic, well-sourced Islamic knowledge and reminders. Values: Sincerity — Teaching and learning for the sake of Allah first.; Patience — Every student progresses at their own pace, without pressure.; Authenticity — Knowledge grounded in reliable sources, not guesswork.; Community — Learning together, supporting one another.

title: What Is Tajweed?
text: Qur'an: Tajweed literally means 'to make better' or 'to improve.' In the context of the Qur'an, it refers to the rules that govern how each letter should be pronounced — including its articulation point (makhraj), its characteristics (sifat), and rules like elongation (madd) and nasalization (ghunnah). Learning Tajweed helps a reciter avoid changing the meaning of the Qur'an through mispronunciation, and is traditionally learned directly from a qualified teacher rather than from text alone, since correct pronunciation is best demonstrated by listening and repeating.

title: The Five Pillars of Islam
text: Fiqh Basics: The five pillars are: (1) Shahada — the declaration of faith, testifying that there is no god but Allah and Muhammad ﷺ is His messenger. (2) Salah — the five daily prayers. (3) Zakat — obligatory charity, typically a portion of savings given annually to those in need. (4) Sawm — fasting during the month of Ramadan, from dawn to sunset. (5) Hajj — pilgrimage to Makkah, required once in a lifetime for those who are physically and financially able. Together, these five acts form the basic framework of Muslim practice, balancing belief, worship, charity, self-discipline, and community.

title: Why Learn Arabic for Qur'an Study?
text: Arabic: While translations convey general meaning, they can't fully capture the layered meaning, rhythm, and grammatical precision of the original Arabic text. Learning even basic Qur'anic Arabic — vocabulary, root words, and simple grammar — lets a student engage more directly with the text, recognize recurring words and themes across the Qur'an, and better appreciate classical tafsir (exegesis), which is written in Arabic. Many students start with Arabic reading (Yassarna-style courses) before moving into grammar and vocabulary specific to the Qur'an.

title: What Is a Hadith?
text: Hadith: Hadith literature complements the Qur'an by recording the sayings, actions, and approvals of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, as preserved by his companions and passed down through documented chains of narrators (isnad). Scholars developed a rigorous methodology to evaluate the reliability of each chain and the plausibility of each report, classifying hadith by authenticity level (such as sahih, hasan, or da'if). This is a specialized field of scholarship — for questions about a specific hadith's authenticity or application, it's best to consult a qualified teacher or an established hadith reference rather than relying on an unverified quote.

title: Sakinah — A Moment of Calm

title: The Garden
text: This isn't a depiction of Paradise — no image or animation could be. It's simply a quiet space to reflect on how the Qur'an describes it. It features live Qur'an verses about Paradise, for reflection, not a literal depiction.

title: Beautiful Stories
text: House of Guidance shares general, well-established stories: Prophet Yunus and the Whale — A story of patience, mistake, and the power of sincere repentance. | Prophet Yusuf's Trials — Betrayal, imprisonment, and eventual honor — a story of patience through hardship. | Bilal ibn Rabah's Steadfastness — An enslaved man's unwavering faith under severe persecution in early Makkah. | The People of the Cave — A group of young believers who fled persecution and were protected in a remarkable way.

title: Path to Marriage
text: House of Guidance offers a respectful, Islamic path for serious Muslims seeking marriage — never a dating platform. Submissions are private and reviewed only by House of Guidance to help facilitate introductions in accordance with Islamic etiquette. This is intended for serious marriage intentions, not casual acquaintance. We encourage involving a guardian (wali) or trusted family member throughout this process. Your information is kept private and is never displayed publicly on this website. House of Guidance will reach out directly if a suitable, mutual introduction is identified.
